scope: Frozen phase-1 single-shot code; diagram and caption are new explanatory artwork, not new simulation results.

a.supports: POST /api/generate previews a generated geometry. POST /api/simulate writes a JSON specification and launches run_batch.py as a subprocess.
Multiple worker processes each execute run_batch.py on a batch JSON specification.
Direct CLI or subprocess entry. Rebuilds geometries, prechecks them, packs viable designs into BatchedSystem and calls AQSRunner. Geometry and numerical settings come from each specification.

Loads the saved family, parameters, seed, device/precision and AQS settings; regenerates a single structure and calls AQSRunner directly. It does not call run_batch.py and is not a guarantee of bitwise replay.
Concatenated positions and structure IDs, with separate orthorhombic cells, atom offsets and per-structure reductions; independent structures share tensors without interacting.

b.supports: Reference-cell relaxation, strain steps, trial and additional minimization, first-damage rollback/bisection, transverse relaxation, recording and per-structure stopping.
Repeated force evaluations with adaptive FIRE steps, periodic neighbor-list rebuilds and force/soft-convergence/failed flags.

Discovery campaign values override generic driver defaults: d_strain_elastic=.01, d_strain=.005, d_strain_min=.00125, max_strain=.32, fmax=.02, stop_stress_fraction=.10, post_peak_strain_limit=.12, max_steps=220.
JSON record, stress_strain.csv, structures and compressed trajectory with per-atom fields. Separate run records/index expose outputs to analysis and browser.
Postprocessing of stress-strain responses and damage; historical endpoint labels need the stopping-rule interpretation already in the manuscript.

c.supports: Screened carbon REBO2 energy and reference-compatible derivative conventions. Autograd computes forces and strain derivatives; per-atom virial is a pair-vector decomposition. CPU/MPS/CUDA selection is in select_device.
Padded periodic neighbor arrays with separate long/short ranges and reverse-pair indices; geometric search occurs on CPU before device tensors are assembled.
Single-structure ASE adapter to the same kernel. ASE stress is volume-normalized, whereas the AQS driver uses area-normalized 2D stress.
Separate planar finite-temperature integrator, Verlet/Langevin, optional fixed engineering strain rate, user-supplied steps and time increment, time/T/energy/stress/position outputs.
Python entry example using both AQS and MD; MD results are written to validation outputs, not automatically to the campaign database.
Finite differences, periodicity, force balance and neighbor tests.
Fixed-state device/precision comparisons with the reference.

abstraction_notes: The dashed bisection arrow combines early and late checks. The full code includes additional minimization and rollback cases.
The FIRE-to-kernel bidirectional connector denotes calls and returned forces/fields; initial and transverse relaxations also query the same kernel.
A kernel neighbor list is reused and rebuilt when required, not rebuilt for every evaluation.
Original limits in the diagram are discovery-campaign settings, not universal library/browser defaults.

Operational stress collapse requires prior bond loss and stress below 10% of the running maximum. The 0.12 post-peak rule also requires prior bond loss; a strictly higher peak updates its strain reference.
Iteration guards and numerical-error branches are omitted graphically. Original controls and validation can have separate specifications.
Nominal FIRE tolerance does not establish actual convergence for every accepted state. Soft acceptance exists and recorded flags require residual review.

Straight-through caps reproduce Atomistica's force convention in over-coordinated environments. The figure deliberately uses 'reference-compatible' rather than making a universal mathematical exact-gradient claim.
The optional MD module is a separate API driver and is not exposed as the browser's AQS simulate endpoint.
AQS output is area-normalized 2D stress. The ASE interface's conventional volume-normalized stress is not conflated with it.
CUDA is a supported code route; it was not benchmarked on the original MPS workstation.
No original code, runs, manuscript, frozen report, manuscript figures or hierarchy follow-up were modified.
